hook: Lotfi Zadeh was born in Baku and later studied in Tehran before completing further degrees at MIT and Columbia University. He spent nine years on the electrical engineering faculty at Columbia before moving to the University of California, Berkeley in 1959, where he later chaired the Electrical Engineering Department from 1963 to 1968 and helped rename it the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences. In 1965 he published the paper Fuzzy Sets in the journal Information and Control, introducing a mathematical framework for representing categories that admit degrees of membership rather than strict true or false boundaries. That single paper launched fuzzy set theory and, later, fuzzy logic, which spread from control engineering into consumer electronics, decision analysis and approaches to reasoning under uncertainty in artificial intelligence. Zadeh remained a prolific researcher at Berkeley for the rest of his career, publishing more than two hundred papers and receiving numerous honors including the IEEE Medal of Honor and the Benjamin Franklin Medal.
